headline: Democrats sweep the US midterms, markets rally hard — MSFT surges 6.7% and PLS jumps 8.9% on the ASX today.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: Pilbara had a cracking session today, up 8.9% to $2.83. The move looks like a broad risk-on rally across the ASX following the US midterm results, plus ongoing speculation about lithium demand recovering. Still deeply underwater overall (down 58% on your cost base) — the long-term lithium story remains unresolved, but today's bounce is a welcome sign of life.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: Take-Two jumped 7.1% last night in the US session, riding the post-midterm market rally. The stock is still slightly below your total invested amount overall, but sentiment around gaming and growth stocks improved sharply as markets cheered a Democrat Congress. GTA 6 hype continues to simmer in the background — Take-Two's CEO was quoted reiterating the studio isn't over-reliant on a single title.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Microsoft surged 6.7% last night — its biggest single-session gain in a while — driven by strong FY27 Q1 earnings released overnight and a broad tech rally after the Democrat midterm sweep. Azure cloud and AI revenue came in ahead of expectations. This puts MSFT well into the green for you, up 25.4% on your cost base. A very strong night.

movers.name: Alphabet Inc. (Google)
movers.note: Google climbed 3.25% last night as the broader NASDAQ rallied post-midterms. The stock also got a boost from optimism that a Democrat-led Congress may take a less aggressive antitrust stance toward Big Tech. Worth noting: OpenAI revealed ChatGPT's search volume is now about one-fifth of Google's — a reminder competitive pressure is real, but Google remains the dominant player.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG rose 1.83% today, carried higher by a strong ASX session (the ASX 200 gained 2.6%) and positive global sentiment following the US midterm results. As a broadly diversified fund it captures the tide across all markets — a good all-round day.

movers.name: BetaShares Diversified All Growth ETF
movers.note: DHHF gained 1.63% today in line with the strong ASX and global market rally. Like VDHG it's a broad diversified fund, so it moves with the market — today's lift was driven by the same post-midterm optimism that swept most global indices.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market Shares ETF
movers.note: VTS added 1.59% today on the ASX, reflecting last night's strong S&P 500 session (+1.6%) following the US midterm results. As a fund tracking the entire US sharemarket, it rises when Wall Street does — solid day.

movers.name: Global X Artificial Intelligence ETF
movers.note: GXAI gained 1.51% today, lifted by the broad tech rally and AI sector optimism. The fund is still down 17.9% on your cost base — AI valuations remain stretched — but the direction today was positive.

movers.name: Vanguard FTSE Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: VGE nudged up 0.52% today — a modest gain compared to the rest of the portfolio. Emerging markets tend to lag when the US dollar strengthens or when investors are chasing US growth stories. The AUD rose slightly today which helps this fund's underlying holdings a touch.

watch_today.title: PLS.AX — Big bounce, but still down 58%
watch_today.detail: Pilbara surged 8.85% today to $2.83, which is great to see, but you're still sitting on an $87 loss against your $150 invested. The lithium market remains difficult — Citi recently cut its lithium price forecasts. For a long-term holder, there's no reason to sell into a dip, and today's bounce is encouraging. Hold and monitor lithium market conditions over the coming months.

watch_today.title: MSFT — Cracking earnings night, up 6.7%
watch_today.detail: Microsoft's FY27 Q1 results blew past expectations last night — Azure and AI revenues were the highlight. The stock is now up 25.4% on your cost base. Nothing to do here except sit tight and enjoy the ride. The long-term AI and cloud thesis is as strong as ever.

watch_today.title: GXAI.AX — AI ETF still underwater despite bounce
watch_today.detail: GXAI gained 1.5% today but remains down nearly 18% on your cost base. The AI sector is growing fast but valuations are still being tested. For a long-term investor, the thesis (AI becomes central to the global economy) remains intact. No reason to sell — the daily move is noise. Hold.

watch_today.title: RBA rate hike — Aussie banks passing it on
watch_today.detail: The RBA raised the cash rate again and Australia's big banks have now passed it on to mortgage holders. The RBA's deputy governor publicly conceded that 'trust in the Reserve Bank is under strain.' This doesn't directly hit your portfolio (no bank stocks) but it's squeezing household budgets and weighing on consumer confidence — worth watching for broader market effects.

watch_today.title: US midterms: Democrats win big — markets cheer
watch_today.detail: Democrats swept the US midterms, flipping both chambers of Congress. Markets rallied hard — the S&P 500 gained 1.6% and the NASDAQ 1.4% last night. Tech stocks in particular surged on expectations of a more regulation-friendly environment for Big Tech. This is a broad tailwind for your US holdings (MSFT, GOOG, TTWO, VTS.AX).

watch_today.title: Iran conflict escalating — Strait of Hormuz incident
watch_today.detail: Iran's Revolutionary Guard reportedly set fire to two tankers and a tugboat in the Strait of Hormuz — a critical shipping lane for global oil. Israel has also told US and Gulf allies that Iran is planning chemical weapons use. Oil is barely moved so far (-0.3% to $87.86), but if this escalates, an oil price spike could stoke inflation and hit global growth. Keep an eye on oil prices this week.

world.summary: The US midterm elections dominated global news today, with Democrats winning big. Meanwhile the Iran conflict is escalating with a serious new incident in the Strait of Hormuz, and Trump faces major decisions about how to respond after his party's election defeat.

stories.title: Democrats sweep US midterms in historic result
stories.why_it_matters: Democrats won control of both the House and Senate in Tuesday's US midterm elections — a thumping result described as a 'sweeping victory.' It's being called a night of firsts, with several historic wins across different states. The result hands Trump's opponents real legislative power and effectively makes him a lame-duck president for his remaining term. Global markets rallied sharply on the news, with the S&P 500 and NASDAQ both jumping over 1.4% last night.

stories.title: Trump says he will accept the midterm election results
stories.why_it_matters: In an interview, Donald Trump said he would accept the results of the midterm elections — a notable statement given his refusal to accept the 2020 presidential election outcome. The midterms were widely seen as a referendum on his presidency and the US-Israel relationship. Iranian leaders were quick to claim the results show American voters have rejected Trump's war policy.

stories.title: Iran escalates: tankers set ablaze in Strait of Hormuz
stories.why_it_matters: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) claimed two oil tankers and a tugboat caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz — one of the world's most critical shipping lanes, through which roughly 20% of global oil passes. This comes as Israel separately told the US and Gulf allies that Iran is planning to use chemical weapons. Reuters reports Trump now faces a stark choice: negotiate a deal with Iran or escalate militarily. Oil is barely moved today, but a serious escalation could send fuel prices surging worldwide.

stories.title: What Trump's midterm loss means for the global economy
stories.why_it_matters: With Democrats now controlling Congress, analysts say Trump's ability to push through tariffs, tax cuts, and deregulation is severely curtailed. The Guardian and Chatham House analysts note this could mean a softer trade policy toward China and allies — potentially good news for Australian exporters who've been squeezed by US-China trade tensions. CommBank's economics team is already updating its forecasts for what a Democrat Congress means for Australia.

stories.title: CVS to break up its $117 billion business
stories.why_it_matters: US healthcare giant CVS — which runs pharmacies, insurance (Aetna) and health clinics — has announced plans to split into separate companies, separating its pharmacy retail arm from its insurance business. The company is worth $117 billion and the breakup is a major corporate story. Shares fell on the news as investors digested the complexity of the split. It signals that giant US conglomerates are under pressure to simplify and show clearer value to shareholders.

markets.summary: A big green day across the board. The ASX 200 surged 2.61% today — one of its better sessions of the year — riding the coattails of last night's strong Wall Street rally after the US midterm results. The S&P 500 gained 1.58% and the NASDAQ 1.44% last night. Gold hit $4,129 USD/oz, oil barely moved, and the Aussie dollar gained slightly, now sitting at 70.2 US cents.

indicators.name: ASX 200
indicators.note: Strong session today — up 2.6% — driven by global risk-on sentiment following the US Democrat midterm win.

indicators.name: S&P 500
indicators.note: Gained 1.58% last night as markets cheered the Democrat midterm sweep, expecting more policy stability.

indicators.name: NASDAQ Composite
indicators.note: Tech stocks rallied solidly last night, with MSFT and GOOG leading gains on earnings and midterm optimism.

indicators.name: Gold (USD/oz)
indicators.note: Gold continues its remarkable run, up 1.4% to $4,129 — investors are still seeking safe havens despite the equity rally, likely due to the Iran conflict.

indicators.name: Crude Oil WTI (USD/bbl)
indicators.note: Oil barely moved despite the Strait of Hormuz incident — markets aren't pricing in a supply shock yet, but watch this space.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: The Aussie dollar ticked up to 70.2 US cents. A stronger AUD slightly reduces the AUD value of your US holdings.

politics.summary: The RBA has hiked rates again and Australian banks are passing the pain straight to mortgage holders. The RBA's own deputy governor is now conceding public trust is eroding. Meanwhile, there's a $506 million headache brewing over the Port of Darwin, and the federal government is under pressure on spending.

stories.title: RBA hikes again — banks immediately pass it on to customers
stories.why_it_matters: The Reserve Bank of Australia has raised the cash rate again and Australia's big banks have immediately passed the full hike onto mortgage customers. The RBA's deputy governor publicly admitted that 'trust in the Reserve Bank is under strain' — a remarkable concession from a central bank official. News.com.au reports borrowers are saying 'it feels like a recession,' with household budgets being squeezed from multiple directions. Higher savings account rates are the one silver lining for those with cash in the bank.

stories.title: $506 million China backflip on Port of Darwin could leave Australia with the bill
stories.why_it_matters: China appears to be backing away from commitments related to the Port of Darwin lease, potentially leaving Australia exposed to a $506 million bill. The Port of Darwin is strategically sensitive — it's the closest Australian port to Asia and near key US military assets. This is another flashpoint in the ongoing Australia-China relationship, and could become a significant political issue given the security implications.

stories.title: Canberra wage bill blowout puts pressure on Treasurer Chalmers
stories.why_it_matters: The federal government's Canberra wage bill has blown out significantly, adding pressure on Treasurer Jim Chalmers to find budget savings. The AFR reports this comes as Chalmers is already under fire — with one opinion piece titled 'Labor's economic model is broken and households are paying the bill.' Albanese is pushing back, redirecting spending scrutiny toward the opposition, but the political heat is building.

stories.title: Australia's teen social media ban has 'modest effect', government tells court
stories.why_it_matters: In court proceedings, the Australian government itself has acknowledged that its social media ban for teenagers has only had a 'modest effect' on young people's political communication. This is a significant admission and raises questions about whether the ban — a flagship Labor policy — is achieving its stated goals. The case is ongoing and could influence how the law is applied or potentially challenged.

ai.summary: The US midterm results are shaping up to be a turning point for AI policy — a Democrat Congress is expected to push for stronger AI regulation. Meanwhile Microsoft's big earnings night highlighted AI as its core growth engine, Tencent launched a major open-source AI model, and Adobe is embedding AI agents across all major platforms.

stories.title: Democrats win midterms — what it means for AI policy
stories.why_it_matters: With Democrats now controlling Congress, the Washington Post's AI & Tech Brief calls it a 'turning of the AI tide.' Democrats are expected to push for stronger federal AI regulation — think mandatory safety testing, transparency requirements, and consumer protections. This could slow some AI deployments but also create more regulatory certainty, which some big tech companies (like Google and Microsoft) may actually prefer over a patchwork of state laws.

stories.title: Microsoft's FY27 Q1 results: AI is the growth engine
stories.why_it_matters: Microsoft dropped its FY27 Q1 results overnight and they were strong enough to send the stock up 6.7%. Azure cloud and AI services were the standout performers, with AI-linked revenue growing significantly. This validates Microsoft's massive bet on OpenAI and its Copilot AI assistant product. It's the clearest signal yet that enterprise AI tools are generating real, measurable revenue — not just hype.

stories.title: Tencent launches Hy4 — a new world-class open-source AI model
stories.why_it_matters: Chinese tech giant Tencent has released Hy4, claiming it joins the ranks of the world's leading open-source AI models — placing it in competition with Meta's Llama and Google's Gemma. Open-source means anyone can download and use it for free. This is significant because it means cutting-edge AI is becoming a commodity available to any developer, anywhere — increasing the pressure on paid AI services and reinforcing China's position as a serious AI competitor to the US.

stories.title: Adobe embeds AI 'coworker' agents across OpenAI, Google, Microsoft platforms
stories.why_it_matters: Adobe has announced its new 'Agentic CX Enterprise Coworker' — an AI agent (think: a digital worker that takes actions on your behalf, not just answers questions) that plugs into AI platforms from Anthropic, Google, Microsoft, OpenAI and others. In plain English: Adobe is building AI workers that can operate inside all the major AI ecosystems simultaneously. This is part of a broader industry shift from AI as a chatbot to AI as an active participant in business workflows — automating tasks that previously needed a human.

sport.summary: The NRL Grand Final is done and dusted — the Roosters edged the Knights 19-18 in a thriller at Accor Stadium. Rugby league lost a legend with the passing of Peter Langmack. The Gold Coast Titans are building for next season, Australia's surfers are heading to Peru, and the AFL is deep in its off-season trade and draft period.

stories.title: Roosters win NRL Grand Final 19-18 over the Knights
stories.why_it_matters: The Sydney Roosters claimed the NRL premiership last Sunday night at Accor Stadium, defeating the Newcastle Knights 19-18 in one of the tightest Grand Finals in recent memory. Just one point separated the two sides at the final siren. It's a premiership for the Roosters and heartbreak for Newcastle.

stories.title: League great Peter Langmack passes away aged 61
stories.why_it_matters: Rugby league has lost one of its own, with the passing of Peter Langmack at 61. Fox Sports reports NRL legend Phil Gould (Gus) paid a heartfelt tribute. Langmack was a well-respected figure in the game. The cause of death has been revealed but details weren't included in the available report. A sad day for the rugby league community.

stories.title: Gold Coast Titans name 11 train-and-trial players for 2027 roster spots
stories.why_it_matters: Your local NRL side, the Gold Coast Titans, have revealed 11 train-and-trial players who are vying for contracts heading into 2027 pre-season. These are fringe players and development prospects hoping to earn a spot on the roster. It's early off-season recruitment news but signals the Titans are actively looking to reshape their squad after the season.

stories.title: Australia's Irukandjis target back-to-back World Surfing gold in Peru
stories.why_it_matters: Australia's women's wheelchair rugby league team, the Irukandjis, are heading to Peru for the World Surfing Championships with sights set on back-to-back gold. Australia is the defending champion and enters as one of the favourites. A good news story for Aussie sport heading into the summer.

stories.title: AFL off-season: six players find new clubs, top draft prospects named
stories.why_it_matters: The AFL trade and free agency period is in full swing with six players finding new homes. The focus is now shifting to the national draft, with top prospects undergoing special testing events. The AFL also confirmed BYD (the Chinese electric vehicle brand) has replaced Nissan as the Hawthorn Hawks' major sponsor — a sign of how Chinese brands are pushing into Australian sport marketing.
